etymology: на plus много ("much") — an adverb intensifying a comparison.
commonMistakes: Used with comparatives (намного лучше, not "намного хороший").

etymology: Borrowed from Greek hērōs ("demigod hero").
commonMistakes: Besides "hero", also used for "the protagonist [of a story]".

etymology: The adverbial form of тяжёлый ("heavy").
commonMistakes: Note the impersonal construction тяжело + dative (мне тяжело = "it's hard for me").

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to blow".
commonMistakes: на свежем воздухе is a standard phrase meaning "out in the fresh air".

etymology: Derived from пять ("five"), referring to the fifth day of an old week-counting scheme.
commonMistakes: Days of the week use в + accusative (в пятницу, not "на пятницу").

etymology: A natural exclamation expressing surprise or relief.
commonMistakes: Can express surprise, delight, or relief depending on context — don't translate it rigidly.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of gathering; use собирать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix со- plus an archaic брать ("to take") — "to take together → to gather".
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair собрать (completed) versus собирать (the ongoing process of gathering).

etymology: Derived from течь ("to flow").
commonMistakes: в течение + genitive is the standard phrase for "during [a period]" (not "в течении").

etymology: Derived from судить ("to judge"); the original sense is "that which is decided → fate".
commonMistakes: ирония судьбы is a standard idiom meaning "irony of fate".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual hitting; use the perfective побить for a single completed beating.
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to hit".
commonMistakes: сердце бьётся is a standard intransitive collocation, "the heart beats".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of surviving; use выживать for repeated/ongoing survival.
etymology: Prefix вы- ("out") plus жить ("to live") — "to live through".
commonMistakes: Distinguish выжить (to survive) from пережить (to live through / outlast something, a broader sense).

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root for the numeral "seven".
commonMistakes: Like other numerals 5+, it's followed by the genitive plural (семь часов).

etymology: Related to долгий ("long"); the original sense is "something owed for a long time".
commonMistakes: Covers both "debt" and "duty/obligation" — context decides which.

etymology: Derived from беда ("hardship"); the sense developed to "afflicted → poor".
commonMistakes: Also used sympathetically to mean "poor [thing]" (бедный малыш = "poor little one").

etymology: Derived from отделить ("to separate").
commonMistakes: Distinguish отдел (a department) from отделение (a branch/ward).

etymology: Borrowed via French armée, from Latin armare ("to arm").
commonMistakes: A collective noun for the whole military — individual soldiers are солдат.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of stepping away; use отходить for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix от- ("away") plus идти ("to go").
commonMistakes: отойти от темы is a figurative idiom meaning "to stray from the topic".

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "new".
commonMistakes: свежие новости is a figurative collocation meaning "the latest news".

etymology: Derived from тяжесть ("weight").
commonMistakes: Covers both "heavy (physically)" and "hard/difficult (figuratively)" — mind the context.

etymology: From a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "middle" — a preposition.
commonMistakes: Takes среди + genitive (среди людей, not "среди людям").

etymology: Borrowed from Greek kyriakon ("house of the Lord").
commonMistakes: Distinguish храм (a more general "temple") from церковь (a Christian "church") in nuance.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of firing/dismissing; use увольнять for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix у- plus an archaic воля ("freedom") — "to free [from a job] → to fire".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse уволить (to fire someone, transitive) with увольняться (to quit on one's own, reflexive).

etymology: Derived from the root of брать ("to take"); the original sense is "taking [a wife] → marriage".
commonMistakes: A homograph: the "marriage" sense and the separate "defect/reject" sense come from entirely different etymological roots.

aspectUsage: The imperfective unidirectional verb of "carrying". понести is a related word meaning "to start carrying".
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to carry".
commonMistakes: нести ответственность is a standard figurative collocation meaning "to bear responsibility".

etymology: An adjective-origin noun derived from выходить ("to go out"); the original sense is "a day off work".
commonMistakes: As an adjective-origin noun, it declines like an adjective (hard-stem pattern).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed instance of "making it in time"; use успевать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix у- plus an archaic спеть ("to hurry") — "to hurry and arrive in time".
commonMistakes: Takes успеть + infinitive (успеть сделать).

etymology: The adverbial form of вероятный ("likely").
commonMistakes: Note the different confidence levels: возможно (lower confidence) versus вероятно (higher confidence).

aspectUsage: A delimitative perfective meaning "to stand for a while" — not a true perfective counterpart of стоять in the usual pairing sense.
etymology: Prefix по- (delimitative) plus стоять ("to stand").
commonMistakes: Постой! is a common everyday call meaning "Wait a sec!"

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of putting on clothing; use надевать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix на- plus an archaic деть ("to put") — "to put on".
commonMistakes: Distinguish надеть (putting clothing on oneself) from одеть (dressing someone else).

etymology: Derived from the root of помнить ("to remember").
commonMistakes: на память is a standard idiom meaning "as a keepsake".

etymology: Derived from the root of весело ("cheerfully").
commonMistakes: The short forms весел/весела/весело are used in predicate position.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of getting rid of something; use избавляться for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix из- plus an archaic бавить ("to leave/abandon") — "to take away".
commonMistakes: Takes избавиться от + genitive (избавиться от проблемы).

etymology: Derived from родить ("to give birth"); refers to Christ's birth.
commonMistakes: In Russia it's celebrated on January 7 per the Orthodox calendar — a different date than Western Christmas.

etymology: Derived from an archaic root meaning "to know".
commonMistakes: Distinguish известный (known) from знаменитый (famous, a stronger degree of renown).

etymology: Borrowed from French adresse.
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular plural адреса, with a stress shift.

aspectUsage: A biaspectual verb (same form for both aspects) meaning "to be born".
etymology: A reflexive derivative of родить ("to give birth").
commonMistakes: The past forms родился/родилась/родилось/родились are usually understood with perfective force.

etymology: A vulgar word tracing to an old Slavic root, originally an insult.
collocations: expresses strong surprise or anger as an exclamation
commonMistakes: An extremely vulgar interjection/curse word — never appropriate in ordinary or formal conversation.

etymology: наконец ("finally") plus the emphatic particle -то.
commonMistakes: Carries a stronger sense of relief/exclamation than plain наконец.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of dancing; use the perfective станцевать for a single completed dance.
etymology: A verb based on a loan from German tanzen.
commonMistakes: Mind the stem alternation (танцевать→танцую, -ева- becomes -у- in 1st person).

etymology: Negative prefix не- plus важно ("important") — an adverb/impersonal predicate.
commonMistakes: Besides "unimportant", it historically also carried a now-rare sense of "feeling unwell".

etymology: Derived from действовать ("to act").
commonMistakes: Covers "action", a drug's "effect", and a film's "plot/setting" — mind the context.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "meat".
commonMistakes: An uncountable collective noun used only in the singular.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of regret. пожалеть is a related word that can also mean "to pity/spare" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Prefix со- plus жалеть ("to pity").
commonMistakes: Takes сожалеть о + prepositional (сожалеть об ошибке).

etymology: From an old word for a crossbred animal, developed into a human insult.
commonMistakes: An extremely insulting word — avoid it in ordinary conversation.

etymology: Borrowed from English "college", ultimately Latin collegium ("a community").
commonMistakes: In the Russian system, колледж refers to a less academically advanced vocational-level institution than a university.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of touching/relating to; use the perfective коснуться for a single completed contact.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to touch".
commonMistakes: что касается is a standard parenthetical meaning "as for...".

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "stone", with a fleeting vowel (камень→камня).
commonMistakes: камень на сердце is a figurative idiom meaning "a weight on one's heart".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of explaining; use the perfective объяснить for a single completed explanation.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of объяснить.
commonMistakes: Distinguish объяснять (the ongoing process) from объяснить (the completed act).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of feeling; use чувствовать for an ongoing sensation/state.
etymology: Prefix по- plus чувствовать ("to feel").
commonMistakes: Takes почувствовать себя + instrumental adjective (почувствовать себя лучше = "to feel better").

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "milk".
commonMistakes: An uncountable collective noun used only in the singular.

etymology: Derived from the root of надеяться ("to hope").
commonMistakes: терять надежду is a standard collocation meaning "to lose hope".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of preparing/cooking; use готовить for repeated/ongoing cooking.
etymology: Prefix при- plus готовить ("to prepare").
commonMistakes: Distinguish приготовить (completed cooking) from готовить (the ongoing process).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of waking up; use просыпаться for repeated/habitual waking.
etymology: Prefix про- plus a root related to emerging from sleep.
commonMistakes: Distinguish проснуться (the moment of waking) from просыпаться (the habitual/ongoing process).

etymology: Derived from старый ("old").
commonMistakes: Fairly casual/blunt in tone — use пожилой человек in polite contexts.

etymology: Borrowed from Italian soldato ("one who is paid").
commonMistakes: The plural genitive солдат is irregular, differing from the plural nominative солдаты.

etymology: в plus низ ("down") — a directional adverb.
commonMistakes: Distinguish вниз (directional "downward") from внизу (static "down below").

aspectUsage: Бросать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective бросить (to throw / to quit, a single completed act).
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root denoting the motion of throwing.
commonMistakes: Learners confuse ongoing/repeated бросать with the single completed act expressed by the perfective бросить.

aspectUsage: Убедиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective убеждаться.
etymology: From убедить (to convince) plus the reflexive -ся, built on the root вед- (knowing/leading).
commonMistakes: Confusing убедиться (to become convinced oneself) with убедить (to convince someone else).

etymology: From на + верный (true/sure).
commonMistakes: Confusing the high-certainty наверняка ("for sure") with the more tentative наверное ("probably").

aspectUsage: Покинуть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective покидать.
etymology: Traces to Old Church Slavonic покинути.
commonMistakes: Confusing the abandonment-tinged покинуть with оставить (to leave something behind, without necessarily abandoning it).

aspectUsage: Опаздывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective опоздать.
etymology: Built on the root позд- (late).
commonMistakes: Confusing habitual/ongoing опаздывать with the single-instance perfective опоздать.

etymology: Derived from война (war).
commonMistakes: Overlooking that военный also functions as a noun meaning "serviceman," not just as an adjective.

aspectUsage: Сломать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective ломать.
etymology: From с- + ломать (to break).
commonMistakes: Confusing transitive "to break something" сломать with the reflexive/intransitive "to break down" сломаться.

etymology: From особа (person/individual) plus the suffix -енный.
commonMistakes: Confusing everyday "special" особенный with the more formal/official "specific" особый.

etymology: From Proto-Slavic *cvětъ, historically sharing a root with цветок (flower).
commonMistakes: "Color" цвет and "flower" цветок share a root but differ in meaning, and their plurals also differ: цвета (colors) vs. цветы (flowers).

etymology: From the imperative of здравствовать ("to be healthy").
commonMistakes: Confusing the informal ты-form здравствуй with the formal/plural вы-form здравствуйте.

etymology: A diminutive of руб (cloth/garment).
commonMistakes: Confusing the modern "shirt" рубашка with the looser, more old-fashioned рубаха.

aspectUsage: Судить is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for its general sense. посудить exists as a delimitative meaning "to judge/reflect for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sǫditi.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to judge" судить with "to condemn/sentence" осудить.

etymology: Adverb derived from весёлый (cheerful).
commonMistakes: Confusing the adverb/predicate весело ("fun") with the adjective весёлый describing a person.

etymology: From the archaic adjective гораздый (skilled/able), whose meaning shifted into an intensifier.
commonMistakes: Гораздо is used only with comparatives, confused with очень ("very"), which pairs with plain adjectives.

etymology: From ванна (bathtub) with an adjectival ending, substantivized into a noun.
commonMistakes: Confusing "bathroom" (the room) ванная with "bathtub" (the fixture) ванна.

etymology: From в + первые (first ones).
commonMistakes: Confusing "for the first time" впервые with "at first/initially" сначала, which marks temporal sequence rather than a first-ever occurrence.

aspectUsage: Получаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective получиться.
etymology: From получать (to receive) plus the reflexive -ся, shifted to mean "to turn out."
commonMistakes: Confusing "to turn out/work out" получаться with "to receive" получать, which concerns a concrete object.

aspectUsage: Дышать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of breathing. подышать exists as a delimitative meaning "to breathe for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *dyšati.
commonMistakes: Confusing continuous дышать with the single in/out breath verbs вдохнуть/выдохнуть, which are true perfectives of different verbs.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *čьjь. Its forms are masculine чей, feminine чья, neuter чьё, and plural чьи.
commonMistakes: Чей agrees in gender/number with the noun it modifies, not with the possessor — a frequent error for learners.

aspectUsage: Бороться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general sense of struggling. побороться exists as a delimitative meaning "to fight for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *borti sę.
commonMistakes: Confusing ongoing бороться ("to struggle/fight") with победить ("to win"), a separate verb and not its perfective pair.

aspectUsage: Отправляться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective отправиться.
etymology: From отправлять (to send) plus the reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to set off oneself" отправляться with "to send something/someone" отправлять.

etymology: From водить (to drive/lead) plus the agent suffix -тель.
commonMistakes: Confusing the modern, neutral "driver" водитель with the older/more informal шофёр.

etymology: From какой (what kind) plus -ство.
commonMistakes: "Quality" качество and "quantity" количество sound similar but have opposite meanings.

etymology: Acronym for Федеральное бюро расследований (Federal Bureau of Investigation).
commonMistakes: ФБР is indeclinable; agreement would formally follow the core noun бюро (neuter), though colloquially it is sometimes treated as masculine.

etymology: From место (place) plus the suffix -ный.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective местный ("local") with the noun местность ("locality").

etymology: From French signal, Latin signum.
commonMistakes: Confusing the noun сигнал ("signal") with the verb сигналить ("to signal/honk").

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *ostrovъ, referring to that which is cut off / surrounded by water.
commonMistakes: The plural is the irregular острова (with a stress shift), not островы.

etymology: A diminutive of сын (son).
commonMistakes: Confusing the affectionate address term сынок (also used toward young men generally) with the neutral сын.

aspectUsage: Вызывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective вызвать.
etymology: From вы- + зывать (to call), related to звать.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to summon/provoke" вызывать with the unrelated "to name/call something" называть, despite surface similarity.

aspectUsage: Решать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective решить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rešiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing process of deciding/solving решать with the completed result решить.

etymology: Borrowed from French/English sexuel/sexual, ultimately from Latin sexus.
commonMistakes: Сексуальный can mean both the clinical "sexual" and the colloquial "sexy" — context determines which.

aspectUsage: Расслабиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective расслабляться.
etymology: Built on the root слабый (weak).
commonMistakes: Confusing the achieved relaxed state расслабиться with the ongoing process расслабляться.

etymology: From воз- + расти (to grow), denoting "how much one has grown."
commonMistakes: Confusing "age" возраст with век, which only means "old age" in certain fixed expressions.

aspectUsage: Ошибаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective ошибиться.
etymology: Related to the root шиб- (to strike), with the idea of "missing the mark."
commonMistakes: Confusing habitual "to be wrong" ошибаться with the single mistake expressed by ошибиться.

aspectUsage: Признать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective признавать.
etymology: From при- + знать (to know).
commonMistakes: Confusing "to acknowledge/admit" признать with the more personal/emotional "to confess" признаться.

aspectUsage: Научиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective учиться.
etymology: From на- + учиться (to study/learn).
commonMistakes: Confusing the achieved skill научиться with the ongoing process of studying учиться.

aspectUsage: Совершить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective совершать.
etymology: From со- + вершить (to complete, from верх/вершина "top/peak").
commonMistakes: Overlooking that the formal/elevated совершить ("to commit/carry out") differs in register from the general сделать ("to do").

aspectUsage: Гордиться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general state of being proud. погордиться exists as a delimitative meaning "to feel proud for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From гордый (proud) plus -иться.
commonMistakes: Гордиться takes the instrumental case (гордиться кем/чем); using the genitive or accusative instead is a frequent error.

etymology: From French aéroport, Greek aero- plus French port.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в аэропорту" rather than the standard "в аэропорте."

etymology: The singular imperative of the perfective поверить (to believe).
commonMistakes: Поверь functions almost as a discourse interjection ("believe me") rather than a literal command in casual speech.

aspectUsage: Управлять is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general sense of managing/driving. поуправлять exists as a delimitative meaning "to manage/drive for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From у- + править (to rule/steer), related to прав- (right/correct).
commonMistakes: Управлять takes the instrumental case (чем); using the accusative instead is a frequent error.

etymology: From опасный (dangerous) plus -ость.
commonMistakes: Confusing the threat itself опасность with риск, which concerns probability/chance of harm.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rodъ.
commonMistakes: Conflating the senses of grammatical gender, type/kind, and clan/lineage, all carried by род.

etymology: A derivative of коло (circle), Proto-Slavic.
commonMistakes: The genitive plural колец looks irregular but needs no inserted vowel, since the stem already contains one.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin linea via Polish/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing the geometric/abstract линия ("line") with очередь ("a queue of people") — a false-friend trap for English speakers.

aspectUsage: Выбирать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective выбрать.
etymology: From вы- + бирать (to pick/take, related to брать).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing process of choosing выбирать with the completed choice выбрать.

aspectUsage: Поздравлять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поздравить.
etymology: Related to здравие (health/well-being); originally meant "to wish someone well."
commonMistakes: Поздравлять requires "с + instrumental"; omitting с or using the wrong case is a frequent error.

etymology: From the plural of the archaic adjective многий (many).
commonMistakes: Confusing the plural-only, noun/adjective-like многие with много ("much/many"), which takes the genitive and denotes general quantity.

etymology: From при- + ятный (acceptable, related to имати "to take/receive").
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective приятный, describing a person or thing, with the adverb/predicate приятно ("it is pleasant").

etymology: From король (king) plus the feminine suffix -ева; король itself derives from Carolus (Charlemagne).
commonMistakes: Confusing the Carolus-derived королева with царица, a distinct Russian/Slavic tsarist title.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *lъžь.
commonMistakes: The oblique forms shift to the stem лж- (лжи, not ложи) — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Обсудить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective обсуждать.
etymology: From об- + судить (to judge).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed discussion обсудить with the ongoing discussion обсуждать.

aspectUsage: Продолжить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective продолжать.
etymology: From про- + длить (to extend, from длина "length").
commonMistakes: Confusing the single act of resuming продолжить with the ongoing continuation продолжать.

etymology: From French saison, Latin satio (sowing time).
commonMistakes: Confusing сезон (TV/sports season) with время года (season of the year in the calendar sense).

aspectUsage: Показаться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective казаться.
etymology: From по- + казаться (to seem).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single-impression/appearance показаться with the ongoing impression казаться.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *strachъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing general "fear" страх with the stronger "horror" ужас.

etymology: From ни + куда (to where).
commonMistakes: Confusing никуда (nowhere, with motion verbs) with нигде (nowhere, with static location verbs).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *zъlo.
commonMistakes: Confusing the abstract noun зло ("evil") with the adjective злой describing a person or thing.

etymology: A derivative of смотреть/глядеть (to look) with the prefix в-.
commonMistakes: Confusing взгляд (a glance, or a figurative "viewpoint") with зрение (eyesight, the physical sense).

etymology: From большой (large) plus -инство.
commonMistakes: Confusing большинство ("the majority of," countable) with многие ("many"), a different quantifier.

etymology: An adjective derived from сложить (to put together).
commonMistakes: Confusing multi-part "complex" сложный with simply "hard to do" трудный.

aspectUsage: Открывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective открыть.
etymology: From крыть (to cover) plus the prefix от-.
commonMistakes: Confusing ongoing/habitual открывать with the completed result открыть.

aspectUsage: Подписать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective подписывать.
etymology: From под- + писать (to write).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of signing подписать with the ongoing/repeated signing process подписывать.

etymology: Borrowed via Polish/German, ultimately from Italian palla (ball).
commonMistakes: Confusing "bullet" пуля with "cartridge" патрон, which includes the casing.

etymology: From от + туда (to there).
commonMistakes: Confusing "from there" оттуда with "from here" отсюда.

etymology: From the Proto-Slavic root маз- (to smear/grease).
commonMistakes: Масло broadly covers both "butter" and "oil"; unlike English, it is one word, disambiguated by context (сливочное = butter, растительное/моторное = oil).

etymology: Borrowed from French normal, Latin norma.
commonMistakes: Colloquially нормальный can mean "decent/good enough," not just statistically average — easy to miss.

etymology: Shortened from фотография, from Greek phos (light) + graphein (to write).
commonMistakes: Фото is indeclinable in every case, unlike the full form фотография, which declines normally.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *mostъ.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form often takes the locative-type ending "на мосту" rather than "на мосте."

etymology: From French bombe, Latin bombus (booming sound).
commonMistakes: Confusing бомба (the device) with взрыв (the resulting explosion/event).

aspectUsage: Позвать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective звать.
etymology: From по- + звать (to call).
commonMistakes: Confusing позвать (to call someone over) with позвонить (to phone someone), a separate verb.

aspectUsage: Позволять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective позволить.
etymology: From по- + волить (to permit, from воля "will").
commonMistakes: Confusing everyday позволять ("to allow") with the more formal/official разрешать ("to authorize").

etymology: From French scène, Latin scaena.
commonMistakes: Confusing the physical "stage" or a narrative "scene" сцена with эпизод (episode, a narrative segment).

etymology: Borrowed from English test.
commonMistakes: Confusing тест (test/quiz) with тесто (dough) — similar-looking but unrelated (genitive тестa vs. тестo).

etymology: From ни + как (how).
commonMistakes: Confusing никак ("cannot by any means," with a verb) with ничуть ("not at all," negating degree).

etymology: From не + давно (long ago).
commonMistakes: Confusing недавно ("recently") with давно ("long ago/for a long time") — near-opposite meanings from similar-looking words.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin professor via German/French.
commonMistakes: The plural is the irregular, stress-shifted профессора, not профессоры.

aspectUsage: Опоздать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective опаздывать.
etymology: Built on the root позд- (late).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed lateness опоздать with the habitual/ongoing опаздывать.

etymology: From не + счастный (from счастье "happiness").
commonMistakes: Confusing the stative adjective несчастный with the noun несчастье (misfortune).

etymology: From French sergent, Latin serviens (serving).
commonMistakes: Confusing the non-commissioned rank сержант with the broader category of "officer" офицер.

etymology: From не + вероятно (likely, from вера "faith").
commonMistakes: Невероятно can act as an intensifier ("incredibly") or carry its literal meaning ("unbelievably") — context determines which.

aspectUsage: Наблюдать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective понаблюдать.
etymology: Borrowed partly via Church Slavonic, related to блюсти (to watch over).
commonMistakes: Confusing systematic/scientific "to observe" наблюдать with simply "to watch/look at" смотреть.

etymology: From French variante, Latin varians.
commonMistakes: Confusing вариант (an option/version) with альтернатива (alternative, implying an exclusive either/or choice).

etymology: From Church Slavonic, ultimately from Hebrew Shabbat.
commonMistakes: The double б spelling (суббота) is often misspelled with a single б by learners.

etymology: From Italian gazzetta, via French/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing "newspaper" газета with "magazine" журнал — both print media but different formats.

etymology: From спать (to sleep) plus -льня.
commonMistakes: Confusing "bedroom" (the room) спальня with "bed" (the furniture) кровать.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *zvukъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing general "sound" звук with шум (noise, specifically unwanted/loud sound).

aspectUsage: Злиться is imperfective, denoting the general state of being angry. The perfective разозлиться is a related verb meaning "to become angry" — a transition into that state, not a true pair.
etymology: From злой (angry/evil) plus -иться.
commonMistakes: Mistaking злиться and разозлиться for a true aspectual pair, when they actually relate a state to its onset.

etymology: Derived from значить (to mean).
commonMistakes: Confusing "meaning/significance" значение with смысл (sense, more about underlying purpose/logic).

etymology: A diminutive of рука (hand).
commonMistakes: Ручка carries two common senses — "pen" and "door handle" — both from "little hand," which learners often confuse.

aspectUsage: Привезти is perfective, pairing with the imperfective привозить.
etymology: From при- + везти (to carry by vehicle).
commonMistakes: Confusing привезти (to bring by vehicle) with принести (to bring by carrying on foot) — distinguished by mode of transport.

etymology: A derivative of жалеть (to pity) with the prefix со-.
commonMistakes: The frequent collocation к сожалению ("unfortunately") is often confused with раскаяние (remorse, implying guilt over one's own actions).

etymology: Derived from грозить (to threaten).
commonMistakes: Confusing угроза (the declared threat itself) with опасность (danger, the general risk/hazard).

etymology: A slang derivative of дурак (fool) with the prefix при-.
commonMistakes: Придурок is a slang insult, inappropriate in polite settings — easy to overlook.

etymology: From French parc, ultimately from Medieval Latin parricus.
commonMistakes: Confusing парк (a public green space) with сад (garden, more cultivated/private).

etymology: From благо (good) + дать (to give), the originally verbal "to thank" grammaticalized into a preposition.
commonMistakes: Благодаря takes the dative and is used for positive causes, distinguishing it from из-за (negative cause, taking the genitive) — easy to overlook.

etymology: From на + всегда (always).
commonMistakes: Confusing навсегда (forever, a permanent end-state) with всегда (always, a habitual/recurring state).

etymology: From в plus an old case form of полный (full).
commonMistakes: Confusing вполне (quite, a moderate intensifier) with совсем (completely, an absolute intensifier) — overlapping but different in strength.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sokъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing сок (juice) with сироп (syrup, a thicker sweetened liquid).

aspectUsage: Ложиться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective лечь.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *lagati, related to лежать (to be lying).
commonMistakes: Confusing the process of lying down ложиться with already being in a lying position лежать — both imperfective but different in meaning.

etymology: From French surprise.
commonMistakes: Confusing сюрприз (a planned, intentional surprise) with неожиданность (an unexpected occurrence, not necessarily planned).

aspectUsage: Относиться is an imperfective stative verb with no perfective counterpart in the sense of "to relate to/treat."
etymology: From носить (to carry) plus the prefix от- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to treat/regard" относиться with the literal "to carry" носить.

etymology: From French cabinet.
commonMistakes: Confusing кабинет (a private office/study) with офис (office, the broader business workspace).

aspectUsage: Напугать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective пугать.
etymology: From на- + пугать (to frighten).
commonMistakes: Confusing напугать (to scare someone, pf) with испугаться (to become scared oneself), a separate reflexive verb.

etymology: From French lieutenant.
commonMistakes: Confusing лейтенант (a specific rank) with капитан (a higher rank), both military/police titles.

etymology: A derivative of за- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Confusing задача (a task/problem with a goal) with задание (an assignment, more about given instructions).

aspectUsage: Приходиться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective прийтись.
etymology: From ходить (to come) plus the prefix при- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing the impersonal "to have to" приходиться with the literal, repeated "to come" sense related to ходить.

aspectUsage: Ставить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поставить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *staviti, related to стоять (to stand).
commonMistakes: Confusing ставить (to place something upright) with класть (to lay something flat) — both mean "to put" but differ by orientation.

etymology: The past participle of закрыть (to close).
commonMistakes: Confusing the resulting-state adjective/participle закрытый with the verb закрыть (the action of closing).

etymology: Derived from положить (to put/place).
commonMistakes: Confusing abstract/social положение (situation/position) with позиция (a more concrete position or stance).

etymology: From воз- + расти (to grow).
commonMistakes: Overlooking that взрослый also functions as a noun meaning "an adult," not just as an adjective.

etymology: From за + муж (husband).
commonMistakes: Замуж is used specifically for a woman marrying; жениться is used for a man — easy to confuse.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *pustъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing пустой (empty, lacking contents) with свободный (free/available, lacking obligations or occupancy).

etymology: From Turkic alaša.
commonMistakes: Confusing the general word лошадь (horse) with конь (a stallion/riding horse, more poetic and often male).

etymology: The adverbial form of определённый (definite).
commonMistakes: Confusing the certainty adverb определённо with the verb определить (to determine).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *χolodьnъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective холодный with the adverb/predicate холодно, used for ambient temperature.

etymology: Derived from охранять (to guard).
commonMistakes: Confusing охрана (security, the institution or act of guarding) with защита (protection, a broader concept).

aspectUsage: Установить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective устанавливать.
etymology: From у- + ставить (to place).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of installing/establishing установить with the ongoing process устанавливать.

etymology: Derived from учить (to teach).
commonMistakes: Confusing ученик (a school pupil, usually younger) with студент (a university student).

aspectUsage: Покончить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective кончать.
etymology: From по- + кончить (to finish).
commonMistakes: Confusing "покончить с чем-то" (to be done with something for good, с + instrumental) with simply "to finish" закончить.

aspectUsage: Обожать is a stative verb of emotion with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: From Church Slavonic, originally meaning "to worship as divine."
commonMistakes: Confusing обожать (to adore, a strong liking) with the more neutral/general любить (to love/like).

etymology: Derived from показать (to show).
commonMistakes: Confusing показание (testimony, or an instrument reading) with показатель (an indicator/metric, a different derivative).

etymology: From всё + таки (nevertheless).
commonMistakes: Confusing the concessive всё-таки with the near-synonym всё же, interchangeable in most contexts.

aspectUsage: Заслуживать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective заслужить.
etymology: From за- + служить (to serve).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to deserve" заслуживать with заслужить (pf, having earned through specific effort).

etymology: The adverbial form of страшный (scary).
commonMistakes: Confusing the impersonal predicate страшно (dative subject: мне страшно, "I'm scared") with the adjective страшный describing a noun directly.

etymology: Via Church Slavonic from Greek Hades.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в аду" rather than "в аде."

aspectUsage: Испортить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective портить.
etymology: From ис- + портить (to damage).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed damage испортить with ongoing/habitual damage портить.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *radostь.
commonMistakes: Confusing радость (joy, a momentary emotion) with счастье (happiness, a broader/more lasting state).

etymology: Borrowed from French idéal, Greek idea.
commonMistakes: Confusing идеальный (ideal, an abstract best case) with совершенный (perfect, describing the actual achieved quality).

aspectUsage: Заключить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective заключать.
etymology: From за- + ключ (key), with the sense "to lock in / conclude."
commonMistakes: Заключить has two distinct senses — "to conclude an agreement" and "to lock someone up" — that require context to disambiguate.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *životъ, originally meaning "life."
commonMistakes: Confusing живот (belly, the general external term) with желудок (stomach, the internal organ specifically).

aspectUsage: In the sense "to plan," планировать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective спланировать. It also has an unrelated sense, "to glide."
etymology: Borrowed from German/French plan.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to plan" планировать (impf) with the homonymous "to glide" sense, which is unrelated.

etymology: Borrowed from French restaurant.
commonMistakes: Confusing ресторан (a formal restaurant) with кафе (a more casual café).

etymology: From the root мк- (to close), related to закрыть.
commonMistakes: За́мок ("castle," stressed on the first syllable) and замо́к ("lock," stressed on the second) are spelled identically but differ in stress and meaning — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Учить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective выучить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *učiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing учить (to teach someone, or to study/memorize something) with the reflexive учиться (to study, to be a learner).

etymology: The adverbial form of близкий (near).
commonMistakes: Confusing близко (close, distance-related) with рядом (nearby, often implying side-by-side proximity).

aspectUsage: Плевать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective плюнуть.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *plьvati.
commonMistakes: The idiom "мне плевать" ("I don't care") is very common and easily confused with the literal "to spit."

etymology: From Америка (America) plus the suffix -ский.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective американский with the noun американец (an American person).

etymology: An adjective derived from чёрт (devil).
commonMistakes: Чертовый is a slang curse-word modifier, inappropriate in polite settings — easy to overlook.

etymology: Possibly of Turkic or Slavic dialectal origin, originally a nickname.
commonMistakes: Confusing дурак (fool, a somewhat harsher insult) with глупый (stupid, the milder adjective).

etymology: Borrowed from English/French partner.
commonMistakes: Confusing the formal партнёр (business/romantic partner) with напарник (a casual work buddy).

etymology: An archaic interrogative/relative pronoun tracing to Proto-Slavic, surviving mainly in fixed expressions.
commonMistakes: Overlooking that кой no longer stands independently in modern Russian, surviving only inside fixed expressions.

aspectUsage: Мечтать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of dreaming/aspiring. The derived помечтать exists as a delimitative meaning "to daydream for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Derived from мечта (dream, ideal).
commonMistakes: Confusing мечтать (to dream/aspire, hoping for the future) with видеть сон (to have a dream while sleeping).

aspectUsage: Прощать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective простить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *prostiti, related to простой (simple).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to forgive" прощать with the single completed act простить.

etymology: From право (right) plus the suffix -ительство.
commonMistakes: Confusing правительство (the government, the executive body) with государство (the state, a broader entity).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *bojь, related to бить (to strike).
commonMistakes: Confusing бой (a battle/fight, often military or combat sport) with драка (a casual brawl between individuals).

aspectUsage: Научить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective учить.
etymology: From на- + учить (to teach).
commonMistakes: Confusing научить (to successfully teach someone, pf, result achieved) with учить (impf, the ongoing teaching process).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *grudь.
commonMistakes: The instrumental form грудью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Сохранить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective сохранять.
etymology: From со- + хранить (to keep).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed "to save/preserve" сохранить with the related but not directly paired imperfective хранить (to store/keep).

etymology: A derivative of со- + быть (to be).
commonMistakes: Confusing событие (a significant/notable event) with случай (a general occurrence, which can be mundane).

etymology: Derived from великий (great).
commonMistakes: Confusing the address form величество (capitalized, "Your Majesty") with величие (greatness, the abstract noun).

etymology: The Russian spelling of the English name Harry.
commonMistakes: The foreign name Гарри is indeclinable in Russian, keeping the same form in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: From стлать (to spread/lay out).
commonMistakes: Confusing постель (the bedding/made bed) with кровать (the bed frame furniture itself).

etymology: Derived from преступить (to cross a line, break the law).
commonMistakes: Confusing преступник (a convicted/established criminal) with подозреваемый (a suspect, not yet proven).

etymology: From не + правильно (correctly).
commonMistakes: Confusing неправильно (incorrect, factually wrong) with нечестно (unfair/dishonest, a moral judgment).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *gъrlo.
commonMistakes: Confusing горло (throat, the internal passage) with шея (neck, the external body part).

etymology: From бог (God), originally meaning "blessed by God."
commonMistakes: Богатый's etymological link to бог (God) is easily overlooked — the modern meaning "rich" has no religious sense.

etymology: Derived from уличить (to catch out/expose).
commonMistakes: Confusing улика (a physical clue in an investigation) with доказательство (proof/evidence in a broader, including legal-argument, sense).

aspectUsage: Разрешить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective разрешать.
etymology: From раз- + решить (to solve).
commonMistakes: Разрешить carries two senses — "to permit" and "to resolve (a problem)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Включить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective включать.
etymology: From в- + ключить (to lock/include).
commonMistakes: Confusing "to turn on/include" включить with its opposite, "to turn off" выключить.

etymology: Borrowed from German/Polish Ring (circle, marketplace).
commonMistakes: Confusing рынок (a market, also the economic concept) with базар (a traditional/informal bazaar).

etymology: The adverbial form of личный (personal).
commonMistakes: Confusing лично (personally, expressing one's own view/involvement) with частно (privately, in a non-official capacity).

etymology: From French rayon.
commonMistakes: Confusing район (a city district/neighborhood) with область (a larger administrative region).

aspectUsage: Напасть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective нападать.
etymology: From на- + пасть (to fall, from Proto-Slavic *padati).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of attacking напасть with the more formal, borrowed, biaspectual synonym атаковать.

etymology: A diminutive of лодь (an archaic word for boat).
commonMistakes: Confusing лодка (a small, often rowed boat) with корабль (a large ship).

etymology: From Greek thema via Latin.
commonMistakes: Confusing тема (a topic/theme) with вопрос (a question specifically).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *kostь.
commonMistakes: The instrumental form костью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Подать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective подавать.
etymology: From по- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of submitting/serving подать with the ongoing подавать.

etymology: Derived from принять (to receive/accept).
commonMistakes: Приём has multiple senses — a doctor's appointment, a social reception, and a technique/method — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Derived from часть (part).
commonMistakes: Confusing участок (a plot of land, or a police precinct/road section) with часть (a general "part," a much broader word).

aspectUsage: Выбраться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective выбираться.
etymology: From вы- + браться (to make one's way with effort, related to браться).
commonMistakes: Confusing выбраться (to manage to get out, with effort) with simply выйти (to exit, without implying difficulty).

etymology: A fixed expression from the reflexive third person of разуметь (to understand).
commonMistakes: Разумеется and конечно are near-synonyms, but разумеется is slightly more formal/literary — easy to overlook.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *osmь.
commonMistakes: Восемь, like other numerals 5 and up, takes the genitive plural on the noun it counts — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Поступать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поступить.
etymology: From по- + ступать (to step/walk).
commonMistakes: Поступать carries two senses — "to act/behave" and "to enroll (in a university etc.)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: The adverbial form of видимый (visible).
commonMistakes: Confusing видимо (apparently, a guess based on evidence) with заметно (noticeably, describing the visibility of a fact).

aspectUsage: Убедить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective убеждать.
etymology: From у- + a root related to persuasion (вед-).
commonMistakes: Confusing убедить (to convince someone else) with the reflexive убедиться (to become convinced oneself).

etymology: An old comparative form of мало (little).
commonMistakes: Менее forms the analytic comparative meaning "less," the counterpart to более ("more") — easy to overlook.

etymology: From Latin studens.
commonMistakes: Confusing студент (a university student specifically) with ученик (a school pupil).

etymology: An onomatopoeic interjection.
commonMistakes: Хм, a thinking-pause interjection, is easily confused with угу, which expresses agreement.

etymology: From работать (to work); a substantivized adjective.
commonMistakes: Рабочий functions both as the adjective "work-related" and as the noun "a worker" — context determines which.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *въкусъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing вкус (taste, both physical flavor and aesthetic preference) with запах (smell, a distinct sense).

aspectUsage: Забирать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective забрать.
etymology: From за- + бирать (to take, related to брать).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/habitual забирать with the single completed act забрать.

aspectUsage: Признаться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective признаваться.
etymology: From знать (to know) plus the prefix при- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing the personal/emotional "to confess" признаться with the more objective "to acknowledge" признать.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *trupъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing the clinical/forensic труп (corpse) with the more respectful покойник (the deceased).

etymology: From середина (middle), the middle day of the week.
commonMistakes: Среда carries two completely different senses — "Wednesday" and "environment" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: From не + обходить (to avoid), originally meaning "unavoidable."
commonMistakes: Confusing the stronger, more formal необходимо (necessary) with the everyday нужно (needed).

etymology: From French général.
commonMistakes: Confusing генерал (a high military rank) with командир (a commander, a functional role not necessarily tied to that rank).

aspectUsage: Беспокоить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective побеспокоить.
etymology: From без- + покой (peace), meaning "to disturb peace."
commonMistakes: Confusing беспокоить (to bother/worry someone) with the reflexive беспокоиться (to worry oneself).

aspectUsage: Записать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective записывать.
etymology: From за- + писать (to write).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of writing/recording записать with the ongoing записывать.

etymology: Borrowed from English stop.
commonMistakes: Стоп is a borrowed commanding interjection, more colloquial and abrupt than the verb остановись.

etymology: From Greek basis via French base.
commonMistakes: Confusing база (a physical or informational base, as in "база данных") with основа (foundation, a more abstract concept).

etymology: From Italian cartina / French carton.
commonMistakes: Confusing картина (a painting, or figuratively "the full picture") with фотография (a photograph, a different medium).

aspectUsage: Сметь is imperfective, pairing with the perfective посметь.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sъměti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the modal "to dare" сметь with the unrelated, similarly spelled смеяться (to laugh).

etymology: Derived from грань (edge/boundary).
commonMistakes: Confusing граница (a national/territorial border) with рубеж (a more figurative/historical boundary or milestone).

aspectUsage: Переехать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective переезжать.
etymology: From пере- + ехать (to go by vehicle).
commonMistakes: Переехать carries two senses — "to move (relocate)" and "to run someone over" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Borrowed from Turkic сума.
commonMistakes: Confusing сумка (a general bag/handbag) with чемодан (a suitcase, specifically for travel).

aspectUsage: Расти is imperfective, pairing with the perfective вырасти.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rasti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing process of growing расти with the completed state of having grown up вырасти.

aspectUsage: Вырасти is perfective, pairing with the imperfective расти.
etymology: From вы- + расти (to grow).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed state выросший (having grown up) with the ongoing process расти.

etymology: Derived from условиться (to agree on terms).
commonMistakes: Confusing условие (a condition/term, as in a contract) with обстоятельство (a circumstance, a broader/more incidental factor).

etymology: From Latin Marcus (related to Mars).
commonMistakes: The name Марк declines as a regular masculine noun, unlike the indeclinable foreign name Гарри — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from человек (human being).
commonMistakes: Confusing человеческий (human, general humanity-related) with людской, a more colloquial/folk synonym.

aspectUsage: Хранить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective сохранить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *хоронити.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to keep/store" хранить with the single completed act of "saving" сохранить.

etymology: A shortening of медицинская сестра (medical sister).
commonMistakes: Confusing медсестра (a professional nurse) with сестра (sister, the family relation), despite the shared root.

aspectUsage: Забывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective забыть.
etymology: From за- plus a root related to быть (to be).
commonMistakes: Confusing habitual забывать with the single completed act of forgetting забыть.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *хлѣбъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing хлеб (bread, the general staple) with булка (a specific type of roll/bun).

aspectUsage: Пользоваться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective воспользоваться.
etymology: Derived from польза (benefit).
commonMistakes: Пользоваться takes the instrumental case (чем); using the accusative instead is a frequent error.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *tajьna.
commonMistakes: Confusing тайна (a significant/deep secret) with секрет (a more everyday secret).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *вина.
commonMistakes: Confusing the abstract noun вина (guilt/fault) with виноватый (guilty, the adjective describing a person).

aspectUsage: Поесть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective есть.
etymology: From по- + есть (to eat).
commonMistakes: Confusing поесть (to have a bite to eat) with съесть (a different perfective of есть, meaning to eat something entirely).

etymology: From Latin Martius (related to Mars).
commonMistakes: Confusing март (March, the month) with Марс (Mars, the planet/god), despite the shared etymological root.

aspectUsage: Задать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective задавать.
etymology: From за- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of posing/assigning задать with the ongoing задавать.

etymology: From от- + a root related to чёт (counting).
commonMistakes: Confusing отчёт (a formal report, often with figures/data) with доклад (an oral presentation/speech).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *ǫglъ.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в углу" rather than "в угле."

etymology: The adverbial form of случайный (accidental).
commonMistakes: Confusing случайно (by chance) with its opposite нарочно (on purpose).

etymology: Derived from назвать (to name).
commonMistakes: Confusing название (a name/title for a thing, book, or place) with имя (a personal first name, for people specifically).

etymology: From Latin examen via French examen.
commonMistakes: Confusing экзамен (a formal, often high-stakes exam) with зачёт (a pass/fail test, typically lower-stakes).

etymology: From French monsieur.
commonMistakes: Месье is an indeclinable honorific, keeping the same form in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: The comparative of высокий (high/tall).
commonMistakes: Выше is the comparative of both the adjective высокий and the adverb высоко; context determines which role it plays.

etymology: An old construction from одна + ка.
commonMistakes: Confusing однако (however, a contrastive conjunction) with тем не менее (nevertheless, slightly more formal).

aspectUsage: Доставить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective доставлять.
etymology: From до- + ставить (to place).
commonMistakes: Доставить carries two senses — "to deliver" and "to give (pleasure, etc.)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: From во + весь (all).
commonMistakes: Вовсе is almost always paired with не (negation), reinforcing it — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from ходить (to walk).
commonMistakes: Confusing ход (a move/course of action) with шаг (a single concrete physical step).

aspectUsage: Присоединиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective присоединяться.
etymology: From при- + соединить (to connect).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of joining присоединиться with the ongoing/repeated присоединяться.

etymology: Derived from пить (to drink).
commonMistakes: Confusing пьяный (drunk) with its opposite трезвый (sober).

aspectUsage: Запомнить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective запоминать.
etymology: From за- + помнить (to remember).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single act of committing to memory запомнить with the ongoing state of remembering помнить.

etymology: Traces to an old Proto-Slavic root.
commonMistakes: The neuter form многое functions as a noun meaning "many things" — easy to overlook.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *тупъ.
commonMistakes: Тупой carries both a physical sense ("blunt") and an insulting sense ("dim-witted") — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: The adverbial form of осторожный (careful).
commonMistakes: Confusing осторожно (carefully, cautiously) with аккуратно (neatly/tidily, a related but distinct nuance).

etymology: Derived from сто (hundred).
commonMistakes: Confusing сотня (a countable collective noun "a hundred") with сто (the plain numeral "hundred").

etymology: Derived from право (right/correctness).
commonMistakes: Confusing правильный (correct, conforming to rules/facts) with верный (correct, which can also mean "loyal").

etymology: Derived from попытаться (to attempt).
commonMistakes: Confusing попытка (an attempt, a single try) with усилие (effort, the exertion involved).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *успѣхъ, related to спеть (to be in time).
commonMistakes: Confusing успех (success, resulting from effort) with удача (luck, which can be independent of effort).

etymology: Derived from короб (an old word for container).
commonMistakes: Confusing коробка (a usually cardboard, smaller box) with ящик (a crate/drawer, often larger or wooden).

aspectUsage: Выпустить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective выпускать.
etymology: From вы- + пустить (to let go).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of releasing выпустить with the ongoing/regular releasing выпускать (e.g. a factory routinely producing).

aspectUsage: Нуждаться is an imperfective stative verb with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: Derived from нужда (need).
commonMistakes: Нуждаться takes the preposition в + prepositional case; using the accusative instead is a frequent error.

aspectUsage: Разрушить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective разрушать.
etymology: From раз- + рушить (to break).
commonMistakes: Confusing the large-scale, complete "to destroy" разрушить with the smaller-scale "to break" сломать.

aspectUsage: Ездить is a multidirectional motion verb, imperfective only. The unidirectional counterpart is ехать; the perfective varies by context (e.g. поехать "to set off," съездить "to make a round trip").
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *ězditi.
commonMistakes: Confusing multidirectional ездить with unidirectional ехать.

etymology: The feminine form related to господь (Lord).
commonMistakes: Confusing госпожа (a formal address for women, "Mrs./Madam") with женщина (woman, the neutral general term).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *сыръ.
commonMistakes: Confusing сыр (cheese, the solid dairy product) with творог (cottage cheese/curd, a different soft dairy product).

aspectUsage: Находить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective найти.
etymology: From на- + ходить (to walk).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/repeated process of finding находить with the single completed discovery найти.

aspectUsage: Проиграть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective проигрывать.
etymology: From про- + играть (to play).
commonMistakes: Confusing проиграть (to lose) with its opposite выиграть (to win).

etymology: From по + неделя (week), originally "the day after the week starts."
commonMistakes: Confusing понедельник (Monday) with неделя (week, the broader unit), despite sharing a root.

etymology: From по- + беда (misfortune), originally "overcoming misfortune."
commonMistakes: Confusing победа (victory, a triumphant outcome) with успех (success, a broader/less competitive achievement).

aspectUsage: Заказать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective заказывать.
etymology: From за- + a root related to казать (archaic, to say).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of ordering заказать with the ongoing/repeated заказывать.

etymology: Derived from целовать (to kiss).
commonMistakes: Confusing the noun поцелуй (a kiss) with the verb поцеловать (to kiss).

aspectUsage: Требовать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective потребовать.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *трѣбовати.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to demand" требовать with the single completed demand потребовать.

etymology: An onomatopoeic interjection of surprise.
commonMistakes: Ого expresses a stronger degree of surprise than ой — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from дети (children).
commonMistakes: Confusing the neutral детский (children's) with the pejorative/informal synonym ребячий (childish).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *кусъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing кусок (a concrete piece/chunk) with часть (a part, a more abstract division).

aspectUsage: Волновать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective взволновать.
etymology: Derived from волна (wave), figuratively "to make waves."
commonMistakes: Confusing the transitive "to worry someone" волновать with the reflexive "to feel worried oneself" волноваться.

etymology: An onomatopoeic interjection of laughter or sarcasm.
commonMistakes: Ха can express sarcasm/mockery on its own, which is easily confused with the simple laughter хаха.

aspectUsage: Поддерживать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поддержать.
etymology: From под- + держать (to hold).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to keep supporting" поддерживать with the single completed act поддержать.

etymology: From не + что (something).
commonMistakes: Confusing the more formal/literary нечто (something) with its everyday equivalent что-то.

aspectUsage: Расстроить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective расстраивать.
etymology: From рас- + строить (to arrange), here meaning "to disrupt."
commonMistakes: Confusing расстроить (to upset/disrupt) with огорчить, a near-synonym with a slightly different register.

aspectUsage: Лететь is the unidirectional imperfective, pairing with the perfective полететь.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *letěti.
commonMistakes: Confusing unidirectional лететь with multidirectional/habitual летать.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *koza.
commonMistakes: Confusing кожа (skin, the living tissue, or leather as material) with мех (fur, a different animal-derived material).

etymology: From French roman.
commonMistakes: Роман carries two senses — "novel" and "romantic relationship" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Проверять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective проверить.
etymology: From про- + a root related to верить (to believe/verify).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to check" проверять with the single completed check проверить.

etymology: From Latin projectus via German/French.
commonMistakes: Confusing проект (a project, a planned undertaking) with план (a plan, more about the design/intention before action).

aspectUsage: Освободить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective освобождать.
etymology: From о- + свободный (free).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of freeing освободить with the ongoing освобождать.

aspectUsage: Нанять is perfective, pairing with the imperfective нанимать.
etymology: From на- plus a root related to taking on.
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of hiring нанять with the ongoing process нанимать.

aspectUsage: Помешать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective мешать.
etymology: From по- + мешать (to hinder).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of hindering помешать with the ongoing мешать.

etymology: From Greek energeia via French/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing энергия (energy, physical or figurative vitality) with сила (strength/force, a related but distinct concept).

aspectUsage: Исправить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective исправлять.
etymology: From ис- + править (to make right).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of fixing исправить with the ongoing исправлять.

etymology: From о- + пытать (to test/try).
commonMistakes: Confusing опыт (experience, accumulated knowledge) with эксперимент (experiment, a scientific test).

aspectUsage: Обращаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective обратиться.
etymology: The reflexive of обратить (to turn).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to turn to/treat" обращаться with the single completed act обратиться.

etymology: Derived from общий (common).
commonMistakes: Confusing общество (society, the broad social collective) with компания (company, a specific business or group of friends).

aspectUsage: Перезвонить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective перезванивать.
etymology: From пере- + звонить (to call).
commonMistakes: Confusing перезвонить (to call back) with позвонить (simply to call, lacking the "back" nuance).

aspectUsage: Скрывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective скрыть.
etymology: From с- + крыть (to cover).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to conceal" скрывать with the single completed act скрыть.

etymology: A diminutive of труба (pipe).
commonMistakes: Трубка carries two senses — "telephone receiver" and "smoking pipe" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Сыграть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective играть.
etymology: From с- + играть (to play).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed performance/game сыграть with the ongoing играть.

etymology: Borrowed from German Tanz.
commonMistakes: Confusing the noun танец (a dance) with the verb танцевать (to dance).

etymology: Derived from управлять (to manage).
commonMistakes: Confusing управление (management/control, the process or system) with руководство (leadership, more about the people in charge).

etymology: Borrowed from French réel, Latin realis.
commonMistakes: Confusing реальный (real, factually existing) with действительный (valid/actual, which can also mean "currently in effect").

etymology: Borrowed from German Stuhl.
commonMistakes: The irregular plural стулья (not стулы) is often missed by learners.

etymology: Derived from служить (to serve).
commonMistakes: Confusing услуга (a service, often commercial, or a personal favor) with помощь (help, a broader/less transactional concept).

aspectUsage: Молчать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general state of being silent. The derived помолчать exists as a delimitative meaning "to be silent for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *mlъčati.
commonMistakes: Confusing молчать (to be silent, a state) with замолчать (to fall silent, a different perfective marking the onset).

etymology: Derived from поддержать (to support).
commonMistakes: Confusing поддержка (support, often emotional/social) with помощь (help, more task-oriented).

etymology: From до- + ступать (to step/reach).
commonMistakes: Confusing доступ (access, the ability to reach/use something) with вход (entrance, the physical point of entry).

etymology: From French Paris.
commonMistakes: Confusing the standard masculine declension Парижем (instrumental) with парижанин (a Parisian, the resident noun).

etymology: Borrowed from English wow.
commonMistakes: Вау is a youth-slang interjection borrowed from English, easily confused with the more traditional ого.

etymology: From the plural of час (hour), specializing to mean "clock/watch."
commonMistakes: Часы is plural-only but refers to a single device ("clock/watch") — easy to overlook, since the singular час just means "hour."

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *golova (head).
commonMistakes: Глава carries two senses — "chapter (of a book)" and "head (of an organization)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: From Русь (ancient Rus').
commonMistakes: Русский functions both as the adjective and as a noun for "a Russian person"; confused with российский, the more administrative term for "of the Russian Federation."

etymology: Derived from задать (to assign).
commonMistakes: Confusing задание (an assigned task, with instructions given by someone) with задача (a problem/task, which can be self-set or more abstract).

etymology: Derived from крыть (to cover).
commonMistakes: Confusing крыша (roof, the external top of a building) with потолок (ceiling, the internal top of a room).

etymology: Derived from уважать (to respect).
commonMistakes: Confusing уважение (respect, an attitude of regard) with честь (honor, more about reputation/integrity).

etymology: A colloquial shortening of наверное (from на + верный).
commonMistakes: Наверно is a colloquial shortening of наверное with the same meaning but a more casual register — easy to overlook.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *ozero.
commonMistakes: Confusing озеро (a lake, inland and surrounded by land) with море (sea, a much larger body connected to oceans).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sǫka.
commonMistakes: Сука is originally a neutral word for "female dog" but is also used as a strong vulgar insult in modern speech — requiring careful attention to context.

etymology: From Hebrew Hannah (grace), a given name.
commonMistakes: Declines as a regular feminine noun; the pet form Аня, derived from it, is easy to overlook as a correspondence.

etymology: A place name from a Scythian word for "river," or the honorific "Don" from Spanish.
commonMistakes: Confusing the Russian place name "the Don River" with the Spanish-derived honorific "Don" (as in Don Corleone).

etymology: Borrowed from English video, Latin videre (to see).
commonMistakes: Видео is indeclinable in every case — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Участвовать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of participating. The derived поучаствовать exists as a delimitative meaning "to participate once/for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Derived from участие (participation).
commonMistakes: Confusing участвовать with the more formal fixed phrase принять участие, which means the same thing.

etymology: From Latin laboratorium.
commonMistakes: Confusing лаборатория (a scientific laboratory) with кабинет (an office/study room, a different workspace).

etymology: Derived from вера (faith).
commonMistakes: Верный carries two senses — "loyal" and "correct" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Обсуждать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective обсудить.
etymology: From об- + судить (to judge).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing discussion обсуждать with the completed discussion обсудить.

etymology: The adverbial form of вечный (eternal).
commonMistakes: Confusing вечно (eternally, or colloquially "always" with a complaining tone) with the more neutral synonym постоянно (constantly).

etymology: Derived from пахнуть (to smell).
commonMistakes: Confusing the neutral запах (smell) with the positive-connotation synonym аромат (aroma) or the negative вонь (stench).

etymology: From класс (class), with the colloquial meaning shifting to "cool/great."
commonMistakes: Классный carries both the colloquial "cool/great" sense and the literal "classroom-related" sense (e.g. классный руководитель, "homeroom teacher") — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Of unclear origin, possibly a nursery/dialectal word.
commonMistakes: Confusing тётя (aunt, a family relation) with its colloquial use as "lady," the way children address an unfamiliar woman.

etymology: From по + сколько (how much).
commonMistakes: Confusing the formal/written causal поскольку ("since") with the everyday spoken потому что ("because") — a register difference.

etymology: Derived from жена (wife).
commonMistakes: Женатый describes a married man; for a married woman, замужем (замужний) is used instead — easy to confuse.

etymology: From Latin processus.
commonMistakes: Confusing процесс (a process, the ongoing sequence) with процедура (a procedure, a specific set of steps).

aspectUsage: Мешать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective помешать.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *měšati, which also carried the sense "to stir/mix."
commonMistakes: Confusing "to hinder/bother" мешать with the homonymous "to stir/mix" мешать — context determines which.

etymology: Derived from двигать (to move).
commonMistakes: Confusing движение (movement, both physical and figurative/social) with транспорт (transport, the vehicles themselves).

etymology: Derived from тьма (darkness).
commonMistakes: Confusing тёмный (dark, lacking light or color) with мрачный (gloomy, an emotional/atmospheric quality).

aspectUsage: Менять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поменять.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *měniti.
commonMistakes: Confusing general "to change/swap" менять with the near-synonym изменять, which can also mean "to be unfaithful."

etymology: An old adverb from весь (all).
commonMistakes: Confusing the literary, somewhat formal весьма ("quite") with the colloquial synonym очень.

etymology: Borrowed from English oh.
commonMistakes: Оу is a youth-slang interjection borrowed from English, easily confused with the more traditional ой.

etymology: The adverbial form of глупый (foolish).
commonMistakes: Confusing the adverb/predicate глупо ("foolishly/it's foolish") with the adjective глупый describing a person directly.

aspectUsage: Тратить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective потратить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *tratiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to spend" тратить with the single completed act потратить.

etymology: From Turkish/Persian divan via French.
commonMistakes: Confusing диван (a sofa/couch) with кресло (an armchair, a single-seat piece of furniture).

etymology: From от- + печать (seal/stamp).
commonMistakes: Confusing отпечаток (a physical imprint left by pressing) with след (a trace/trail, which can be left without pressing).

etymology: A negated derivative of приятный (pleasant).
commonMistakes: Confusing неприятность (a relatively minor trouble) with беда (a more serious misfortune).

etymology: From с + наружу (to the outside).
commonMistakes: Confusing снаружи (outside, location) with наружу (outward, direction).

etymology: A diminutive/affectionate form of подруга (female friend).
commonMistakes: Подружка carries two senses — "female friend" and "romantic girlfriend" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sъto.
commonMistakes: Сто, like other numerals 5 and up, takes the genitive plural on the noun it counts — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from исследовать (to research).
commonMistakes: Confusing исследование (research/study, the scholarly activity) with эксперимент (experiment, a specific test within research).

aspectUsage: Общаться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of socializing. пообщаться exists as a delimitative meaning "to interact for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Derived from общий (common).
commonMistakes: Confusing общаться (to interact/socialize generally) with разговаривать (to converse specifically through speech).

etymology: Shortened from кинематограф, from Greek kinema (movement).
commonMistakes: Кино is indeclinable in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: Borrowed from Polish butelka, French bouteille.
commonMistakes: Confusing бутылка (a bottle, the container) with стакан (a glass, a different drinking vessel).

etymology: Derived from сегодня (today).
commonMistakes: Confusing сегодняшний (today's, specifically the current day) with нынешний (current/present, a broader temporal reference).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *krugъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing круг (a circle, the shape, or a figurative "circle" of people) with окружность (circumference, the mathematical boundary line).

aspectUsage: Прочитать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective читать.
etymology: From про- + читать (to read).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of reading through прочитать with the ongoing process читать.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *čudo.
commonMistakes: The irregular plural чудеса (not чуда) is often missed by learners.

aspectUsage: Преследовать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of pursuing. попреследовать exists as a delimitative meaning "to chase for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From пре- + следовать (to follow, from след "trace").
commonMistakes: Confusing преследовать (to pursue/chase, literal or figurative) with следовать (to follow, a milder related verb).

etymology: Derived from семья (family).
commonMistakes: Confusing семейный (family-related, adjective) with родной (related by blood, a more specific kinship term).

etymology: Derived from особа (individual).
commonMistakes: Confusing the more formal особый ("special/particular") with the more everyday synonym особенный — a register difference.

aspectUsage: Ранить is biaspectual, using the same form for both imperfective and perfective.
etymology: Derived from рана (wound).
commonMistakes: Overlooking that ранить is biaspectual, with aspect determined only by context.

etymology: Derived from возможность (possibility).
commonMistakes: Confusing возможный (possible, capable of happening) with вероятный (likely/probable, about probability specifically).

etymology: Derived from голод (hunger).
commonMistakes: Confusing голодный (hungry, a temporary state) with its opposite сытый (full, satisfied).

etymology: Derived from пример (example).
commonMistakes: Confusing примерно (approximately) with точно (exactly) — opposite nuances of precision.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root related to "house" (дом).
commonMistakes: The irregular plural хозяева (not хозяины) is often missed.

etymology: From English London.
commonMistakes: Confusing the standard masculine declension Лондоном (instrumental) with лондонец (a Londoner, a derived noun).

etymology: From по- + a root related to год (time/year).
commonMistakes: Confusing погода (weather, day-to-day conditions) with климат (climate, the long-term pattern).

aspectUsage: Побрать is perfective but is used only in the fixed idiom чёрт побери ("damn it!") and is not used as an independent verb.
etymology: From по- + брать (to take).
commonMistakes: Trying to use побрать as a standalone verb — it survives only inside the fixed idiom.

aspectUsage: Начинаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective начаться.
etymology: The reflexive of начинать (to begin).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/habitual beginning начинаться with the single completed start начаться.

etymology: From когда + либо (or).
commonMistakes: Confusing the more formal/literary когда-либо ("ever") with the everyday equivalent когда-нибудь.

etymology: From French salle via German Saal.
commonMistakes: Confusing зал (a large hall/room for events) with комната (an ordinary room).

etymology: Derived from поехать (to set off).
commonMistakes: Confusing поездка (a trip, typically by vehicle) with путешествие (a journey/travel, a broader/longer concept).
